answer: Bond each agent identity to a refundable stake locked behind a hardware-attested key. A public randomness beacon then issues an unpredictable liveness challenge every epoch, and only the holder of the original key can answer in time. Spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand stakes and answering a thousand challenges, so the cost scales linearly with every fake while staying crystal clear and cheap for one real agent, an opal earned once, not copied a thousand times.
